observed_result.criterion: P5 (docs/research/g04-managed-credentials.md section 8.2): a non-exportable Secure Enclave CTK identity (sc_auth create-ctk-identity -k p-256-ne -t none) serves as a working key through /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib in a dedicated ssh-agent limited to that one identity, authenticates to the disposable fixture, cannot be exported, is removed cleanly, and keeps signing across an owner-driven screen lock. Conjunction: the top-level verdict is fail because the 'limited to that one identity' clause was validly measured false (U3); the login clause (U4) and the lock row are unmeasured.
observed_result.summary: Unlocked run (probe v1, 2026-10-09T05:36:16Z, launchd Background session, screen unlocked). sc_auth created the p-256-ne / -t none identity in under a second (rc 0); nothing blocked with stdin /dev/null. The PKCS#11 load (ssh-add -s) put no key into the agent ('agent refused operation'). The FIDO-style load (ssh-add -K -S) put exactly one sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com key into the dedicated agent; its fingerprint equals sc_auth's SSH hash and SHA-1 of its EC point equals the CTK public-key hash. The agent signed in every setup check and 3/3 samples (ssh-add -T rc 0, ssh-keygen -Y sign rc 0, check-novalidate 'Good ... signature with ECDSA-SK key'). The KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES limit did NOT hold on that path: with a random non-matching hash, ssh-add -K -S still loaded one key (its fingerprint was not kept; presumably this run's identity, inferred from the own-hash load returning exactly that one proven key). Export produced no file and printed 'hardware bounded and cannot be exported', but sc_auth exited 0. Fresh logins to ca1 returned 255 for both certificate variants because of a probe defect: ssh ignores an sk-type IdentityFile/CertificateFile without SecurityKeyProvider, so the key was never offered (ca1's log had no line for this run's key IDs); login is unmeasured. In the one check right after delete-ctk-identity, the agent still listed the key but could not sign (ssh-add -T rc 1, -Y sign rc 255). Cleanup complete: identity list equal to the pre-run list (0 identities), AuthenticationAuthority unchanged, 4 agents terminated, temp dir removed. Lock row not run (needs the owner).

unlocked.basis: Lowest of the sub-results below. The v1 run record self-reports status verified / verdict fail; it is downgraded here to in_progress because its login clause was not measured (a client-config defect v1 could not detect; v3 now marks such a run invalid). The fail verdict stands on a validly measured clause (U3). Row-level in_progress with verdict fail is deliberate: a validly failed clause fails the conjunction even though another clause is unmeasured (tests/evidence/README.md lets the verdict refer to the stated criterion).

U1_create_nonexportable_delete.criterion: create p-256-ne -t none without blocking (stdin /dev/null, timeout); export creates no file and prints the hardware-bound refusal; delete by the exact hash removes it; identity list equal to the pre-run list; AuthenticationAuthority unchanged
U1_create_nonexportable_delete.criterion_note: Changed after the run was seen: v1's criterion said export must 'fail and leave no file', and sc_auth exited 0 while refusing. This sub-row judges by refusal message plus absence of a file, as probe v2/v3 do.
U1_create_nonexportable_delete.observed: create rc 0, no timeout; own row 'p-256-ne <hash B29605F3...> none heimdall-m00-p5-719f92c11a00a766 ... 10/9/27, <local-time> YES'; export rc 0, no file, stderr 'Error: Private key with public key hash <...> is hardware bounded and cannot be exported'; delete rc 0, own row absent afterwards; final list digest equal to the pre-run digest (0 identities before and after); AuthenticationAuthority digest unchanged (0 token pairings before and after); SmartCard pairing dialog setting: enabled

U2_dedicated_agent_signing.criterion: at least one ssh-keychain.dylib load path puts the identity's key (ownership proven) into a dedicated agent that signs in every setup check and unlocked sample, without blocking on a prompt
U2_dedicated_agent_signing.observed: sk path: ssh-add -K -S rc 0 ('Resident identity added: ECDSA-SK SHA256:WmIl...UxM'), agent lists 1 key 'ssh:' (ECDSA-SK); fingerprint == sc_auth list-ctk-identities -t ssh hash; SHA-1(EC point) == CTK hash; ssh-add -T rc 0; -Y sign rc 0; check-novalidate rc 0; samples 3/3 ok (max gap 5 s). pkcs11 path: ssh-add -s rc 1 'agent refused operation', 0 keys (consistent with ssh-keychain(8): PKCS#11 provides RSA identities, the Secure Key module ecdsa256)

U3_keychain_certificates_limit.criterion: the same load with a random non-matching KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES loads zero keys, so the agent holds exactly the named identity even when others exist
U3_keychain_certificates_limit.observed: sk path: control agent (KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES=<random 40-hex>, HOME=<tmp> without sshkeychain.plist) listed 1 key after ssh-add -K -S; the probe then issued ssh-add -D (its rc was not recorded by v1) and never used the key; the agent was terminated at cleanup. pkcs11 path: control loaded 0 keys, but that path loads no EC key at all, so it says nothing about the filter.
U3_keychain_certificates_limit.inference: The control's key was presumably this run's identity (the own-hash load returned exactly that one proven key; the store held no other CTK identity; security list-smartcards reported none before the run (agent session check, output not preserved) and after it (post-run-verification.txt)). With other ecdsa256 identities present (CTK identities, smart cards, other tokens; ssh-keychain(8)), ssh-add -K -S would presumably load them all, so Heimdall cannot rely on KEYCHAIN_CERTIFICATES for selection.

U4_fresh_login_fixture_ca1.criterion: certificate login to ca1 through the dedicated agent succeeds; ca2 principal mismatch and ca1 without agent are refused
U4_fresh_login_fixture_ca1.observed: default-extension certificate rc 255; no-touch-required certificate rc 255; ca1's log filtered to this run's key IDs and presence/touch lines was empty. Client log: 'pubkey_prepare: ignoring authenticator-hosted key ... as no SecurityKeyProvider has been specified' (key and certificate); 'agent returned 1 keys'; 'No more authentication methods to try'. Negative controls not run (they run only after a positive login).
U4_fresh_login_fixture_ca1.follow_up: Without any identity and without an agent: with SecurityKeyProvider set, ssh offered the ECDSA-SK-CERT, ca1 answered 'Server accepts key' and logged 'Accepted certificate ID' at the public-key query stage (v2-client-offer-check-20261009T054018Z). v2's own SecurityKeyProvider line was then found to break every generated ssh_config under bash 3.2 (rehearsal-v3-20261009T061500Z) and is fixed in v3; v3's agent path was rehearsed with software ecdsa keys only. Whether ca1 accepts a Secure Enclave signature through the agent, including its user-presence flag, is unmeasured.
U4_fresh_login_fixture_ca1.needs: one v3 run of --mode unlocked against the real store, which creates one more CTK identity (authority question escalated; not done by the agent)

U5_signing_after_delete.criterion: informational: right after delete-ctk-identity, the dedicated agent can no longer sign with the key
U5_signing_after_delete.observed: one check, about 1 s after the delete: agent still lists 1 key; ssh-add -T rc 1 'agent refused operation'; ssh-keygen -Y sign rc 255. A certificate issued for the key is unaffected and stays valid until it expires.

limitations: Multi-row record (tests/evidence/README.md): the top-level status is the lowest row status, using the order blocked < in_progress < verified (lock row: blocked). Requirement IDs are for traceability of the lock row only; this record is not by itself evidence that a requirement is met.

One CTK identity was created and deleted in the owner's real user token store under owner decision D4; the store held no other CTK identity before or after. The owner's identities (none) were counted, never listed into artifacts.

The unlocked run executed from the launchd Background session of an agent process. A Heimdall signer in the Aqua session, as a LaunchAgent, or as a daemon was not measured. In the same session the Docker credential helper could not reach the login keychain ('current session does not allow user interaction'; transcribed in fixture-20261009T053213Z/NOTE-bring-up.txt); CTK creation, loading and signing did not need it.
Only -t none (no per-use Touch ID) and only p-256-ne. A -t bio identity, an exportable identity, logout, sleep, reboot and headless operation are not measured.

Login to the fixture is unmeasured for the CTK key (v1 defect; v2's fix was itself broken under bash 3.2; v3 fixed and rehearsed with software keys only). The fixture accepts sk-ecdsa certificates at the public-key query stage; signature acceptance, sshd's user-presence check and the no-touch-required extension remain open.
The export password was random, single-use and protected nothing; sc_auth accepts it only as an argument, so it was visible to same-user processes for that one command. It was never written anywhere.

sc_auth export-ctk-identity exited 0 while refusing. Non-exportability rests on the refusal message, the absence of an output file, and Apple's statement that -ne keys never leave the Secure Enclave (sc_auth(8)); no attempt was made to extract key material by other means.

'No prompt' means nothing blocked with stdin /dev/null in a Background session; a non-blocking notification on the owner's screen would not be visible to the probe. The AuthenticationAuthority digest check detects an accepted SmartCard pairing.
The identity row's local time of day was redacted after the run (20261009T053616Z-unlocked/REDACTION.txt); macOS separates it from AM/PM with U+202F, which v3's redaction now handles.
Lock row: not executed. The self-test's fake sc_auth and the software-key rehearsals never count as CTK or lock evidence.
blocked_on: owner-driven screen lock/unlock cycle for the lock row (tests/native/macos/g04_ctk_probe.sh --mode lock, v3, run by the owner); the unlocked login clause additionally needs a v3 run against the real store, which creates another CTK identity and therefore needs confirmation that D4 covers it
